html:
Violeta Parra was a Chilean singer, songwriter, folklorist and artist, the mother of the Nueva Canción, the New Song movement of Latin America. Her best-known song is Gracias a la vida, Thanks to Life.

From a poor rural family, she travelled the countryside of Chile from the 1950s collecting thousands of old songs and verses from peasant singers. She also wrote her own songs about poverty and injustice, and made embroidered tapestries shown at the Louvre in 1964.

She took her own life in 1967. Her children and younger musicians such as Víctor Jara carried on the New Song, which joined folk music to left-wing politics and became the soundtrack of the years of Allende. After the coup it was banned and sung in exile, and her songs spread across the world.
